title: Fantasy RPG powered by real world activity
author: tr99house123
selftext:
Heya, I used to be an avid gamer but life happens and time is spent for other things. Thirst is still there so I am making a mobile game which respects your time and rewards you for living well. Art style is inspired by Black Desert Online, Elder Scrolls Online etc. instead of pixel or cutesy graphics.

It converts calories burned IRL into energy which you use to explore a spiritually hollow world.

I am attaching a video of Essence collection in your base which you can slowly evolve to gain more functionalities.

Curious to hear your thoughts on game concept.

Thanks in advance for your responses.

AI is used for coding help and image generation.

comments.author: holdmyspot123
comments.body:
I encourage you to re-write everything on this yourself, because the concept and art is really pretty and nice. It is jarringly AI written, but the thing is, is the basic text and idea is literally already there, so you can easily so that yourself. Have it organize all of the text to be rewritten and serve it to you in bite sized chunks, re-write it, and have it plug the chunks back in. Or however you want to do.

Secondly, I know you want to be taken seriously. But have fun! And if the theme is activity make a dual visual theme of the pretty-pretty and activity! Because right now I feel like I am pressing start on a text based fantasy adventure game. 

This is so good I really like it!

replies.author: tr99house123
replies.body: Hey, believe it or not I wrote the text myself 😁 So glad you like the concept though. I am experiencing with different styles of videos. I have tried the real life activity transition into game and it did not land that well since most people scroll fast and if they see IRL activity footage in a place where it’s about games it confuses them.

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: Haha that's kinda cool.  Literally fuel your gaming habit with exercise.  Good work

replies.author: tr99house123
replies.body: Never thought about it in that way but you are right, the boundary dissolving in the other direction. That reframe is going to stick with me for sure, thanks!
